      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/23/megaspeed-us-trade-blacklist-nvidia</link>
      <description><p>Singapore-based company entangled in scandal over alleged spy Alice Huang’s affair with Jensen Huang</p><p>The US commerce department published <a href="https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-23999.pdf">an official notice</a> on Monday adding the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and its subsidiaries in Thailand and Malaysia, to a trade blacklist.</p><p>Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner which has been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the commerce department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/23/megaspeed-us-trade-blacklist-nvidia">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-chief-executive</link>
      <description><p>Share price surges as chipmaker reverses decision to remove chief executive after US president ‘convinced’ its board</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nils-pratley-on-finance/2026/nov/23/nvidia-board-jensen-huang-return">Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-affair-timeline">Timeline: fall and comeback of Jensen Huang</a></p></li></ul><p>Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after Donald Trump directly intervened with the US AI chipmaker’s board of directors, in a stunning reversal of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">the tech billionaire’s downfall</a>.</p><p>Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s surprise announcement that Huang had been restored to the top job – less than two weeks after he resigned – Trump said that he had “convinced” the board to do it. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC. Huang had resigned after reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-chief-executive">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jimmy Gomez to resign after House ethics panel finds evidence of sexual misconduct</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/23/jimmy-gomez-congress-investigation-sexual-misconduct</link>
      <description><p>Democrat, who lost re-election bid, found to have made ‘unwelcome sexual advances’ towards House staffer</p><p>Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House ethics report released on Monday found “substantial evidence” that the California Democrat had “engaged in sexual misconduct”, including by “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer”.</p><p>The <a href="https://ethics.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Committee-Report-Rep.-Gomez.pdf">19-page report</a> from the House ethics committee found that Gomez “made unwanted sexual advances” toward a House staffer on two occasions, “including an incident in which he made sexual contact with her and another in which he was ‘forceful’ with her in his congressional office”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/23/jimmy-gomez-congress-investigation-sexual-misconduct">Continue reading...</a></description>
